The tower's coming down! Everybody out — that includes you, Lord-Commander.
I'll walk. I'll not be carried out of my own Lantern by a squire.
Bram: Knight. Sir Bram Kestrel.
Garrick: Hm. And who dubbed you?
Bram: A deserter.
Garrick: Ha. Of course he did.
Bram: Then walk.

The Grand Lantern. Bram fought Garrick alone. He went down twice and got up twice. He didn't kill him. Garrick gave us the Shard and walked out on his own. Bram's hands didn't stop shaking for an hour. He says that's the trick.
Pressed between two volumes of liturgy: a child's drawing. Two stick figures under an enormous yellow sun. The tall one is labeled CASS. The small one is labeled ME.
Underneath, in a grown man's careful hand: _Lysa, age 7._
...She drew the sun too big.
Everybody draws the sun too big when they're seven.

A Choir ledger. Columns of names from the Undercroft, each with a date and a single word beside it: _Offered._ At the foot of every page, the same initials, in the same careful hand as the drawing: C.L.
He knew. About Mercy. About the Undercroft. He signed every page.
He dismissed her in front of the whole city.
He's always very kind in front of people.
The Halcyon moors at the end of the old dock. The dock hangs over nothing now.
This is where she stood. This is where she gave you Dad's compass, and told you to go.
...I came back. I'm late.
That was not her. That was the island remembering her.
The whole island is doing it. Look. The square. The well.
The Lantern's still burning. Up on the bluff.
She's up there.
Then we walk up. Nobody's in a hurry, sparrow. Not here.
Lanternfall. The dock hangs over nothing. The island is remembering things. It remembered Mom saying "come back to me." I did. A year late.
Up on the bluff, the light in the Lantern's doorway thins, like a held breath let out.
The village well. WREN + ILSE + THE SEA. The W is backwards. It always was.
Little Ilse
You did the W backwards.
Little Wren
It's _stylish_. When I'm famous everyone'll do their W's like this.
You're not going to be famous. You're going to be a Keeper like your mum.
I'm going to sail to the end of the world and come back with a sea monster.
...Can I come?
Obviously. Somebody has to carry the bandages.
We were seven.
I did come back with a sea monster. Sort of. Brinefang counts.
It doesn't count, you didn't bring it back.
The memory sours at the edges, the way milk turns — and the well vomits up black water, and the water has hands.
For the record, I still have the bandages.
Home. The east wall is gone; the sky looks in. Everything else is exactly where it was. Two plates on the table.
I left the table. I didn't even finish supper. That was the last supper we ever had, and I didn't finish it.
Outside, something is scratching at the door. Something that came up out of the sea on a stormy night, a long time ago, and never really left.
Two plates. She kept setting two plates. For seven years. Even after Dad.
No. Not for Dad. For me. One for her and one for me.
Your mother's herb garden. Rosemary gone to ash. Thyme gone to ash.
And the sea-lavender — the one that never flowered in all the years you knew it — is covered in small purple flowers.
...Now? Now you flower?
Perhaps it was waiting for someone to come home and see.
The lamp room of Lanternfall. The light is everywhere — in the walls, in the floor, in the air like warm water.
At the heart of it, with her back to you and her hands lifted to the lamp, a woman in a Keeper's robe. Her braid has come undone. The light pours out of her hands and does not stop.
Wren. You're late for supper.
Come inside, little bird. It's getting dark. It's been getting dark for such a long time.
Mom, you can let go now. The boat got away. We made it. I made it. It's been a whole year.
If I let go, the dark comes in.
If I let go, you'll leave. You always wanted to leave. You used to toddle to the end of the dock and just _look_.
In Wren's pack, the little brass lantern her mother gave her flares, as if it has recognized someone.
Stay. I'll keep the light on. Nothing will take you. Not the sea. Not the Hierophant. Not _time_. You'll be sixteen forever, and I will never have to watch you go.
Wren. That is what he wants. That is Evernoon.
...She's not wrong, though. That's the worst part. Some days it's what I'd want too.
